tools.name: maintenance_calories
tools.description: Estimate daily maintenance calories (Mifflin-St Jeor × activity multiplier) for an adult.

tools.name: bulking_calories
tools.description: Maintenance calories plus the 10–15% lean-gain starting surplus and a weekly gain guide (the Bodywise bulking calorie calculator).

tools.name: calorie_calculator
tools.description: Older calculator kept for backwards compatibility: maintenance (Mifflin-St Jeor × named activity level) times 0.80, 0.85, 1.00 or 1.10 by goal. It has no Bodywise page. tools.name: daily_protein_range
tools.description: Daily protein of 1.6–2.2 g per kg bodyweight and the per-meal split (the public Bodywise protein calculator page, /hub/protein-calculator). Prefer this over protein_calculator when matching the website.

tools.name: protein_calculator
tools.description: Older goal-based daily protein range (fat_loss, hypertrophy, maintenance, endurance; optional lean mass), kept for backwards compatibility. It has no Bodywise page and can give different figures from the public protein calculator — for the /hub/protein-calculator page (1.6–2.2 g/kg) call daily_prote

tools.name: macro_calculator
tools.description: The public Bodywise macro calculator page (/macro-calculator): maintenance calories (Mifflin-St Jeor × activity multiplier), a goal target (build +300 kcal, maintain 0, lean −400; never below 1,200 kcal) and daily protein, fat and carb grams. No email is needed or accepted.

tools.name: protein_distribution_calculator
tools.description: Split a daily protein target across meals and compare each meal with 0.4 g per kg of bodyweight.

tools.name: one_rep_max
tools.description: Estimate a 1RM (Epley, counting reps in reserve) and working weights from a completed set.

tools.name: rpe_rir_calculator
tools.description: Working weight for a target number of reps at a target RPE or reps in reserve (Epley model).

tools.name: fat_free_mass_index
tools.description: Calculate fat-free mass, FFMI and height-normalised FFMI (Kouri et al., 1995).

tools.name: fat_loss_timeline_calculator
tools.description: Projected weeks and daily deficit to reach a target body-fat percentage, assuming all loss is fat (~7,700 kcal/kg).

tools.name: lift_balance_calculator
tools.description: Squat, deadlift and overhead press as percentages of bench press. Descriptive only.

tools.name: dots_wilks_calculator
tools.description: DOTS (IPF 2019) and original Wilks scores for a powerlifting total at a given bodyweight.

tools.name: creatine_dosing_calculator
tools.description: Creatine monohydrate maintenance (3–5 g/day) and optional loading dose (~0.3 g/kg/day for 5–7 days).

tools.name: ipf_gl_points_calculator
tools.description: IPF GL points (IPF 2020 classic three-lift coefficients) for a squat + bench + deadlift total at a given bodyweight.

tools.name: strength_to_bodyweight_calculator
tools.description: Each lift as a plain multiple of bodyweight. Descriptive only; it never labels a lifter's level.

tools.name: barbell_warm_up_calculator
tools.description: Warm-up sets at about 40, 55, 70 and 85% of a working weight, then the working weight, with plates per side (plates 25–1.25 kg).

tools.name: lean_bulking_rate_calculator
tools.description: Weekly and monthly weight gain at 0.25–0.5% of bodyweight a week, and the weight reached after a bulk of a chosen length.

tools.name: double_progression_calculator
tools.description: Double progression: from the reps completed in each working set today, returns the weight and rep target for the next session. Weight only goes up once every set reaches the top of the rep range.

tools.name: dumbbell_barbell_converter
tools.description: Converts dumbbell and barbell loads. The total is arithmetic for any lift. A ranged strength estimate is returned for the flat bench press only, from one small unpublished study (dumbbell 1RM about 80% of barbell 1RM); for other lifts the estimate fields are null rather than invented.

tools.name: weekly_volume_auditor
tools.description: Describes weekly hard sets per muscle group against the roughly 10-or-more weekly sets the 2026 ACSM position stand favoured. Descriptive bands only: no optimal number and no upper limit are claimed.

tools.name: rest_between_sets_calculator
tools.description: A rest window in seconds for an exercise type and goal, with the evidence caveats. Not a proven optimum.

tools.name: bulking_stall_calculator
tools.description: Compares weekly weight change with a 0.25-0.5% of bodyweight a week monitoring range and suggests a calorie step. Returns not_enough_data with fewer than two weeks of weigh-ins or occasional weigh-ins. Never diagnoses a medical cause.

tools.name: fat_calculator
tools.description: Daily fat: 0.8 g per kg bodyweight by default (allowed 0.5–1.2 g/kg). Optionally give daily_kcal to see the % of calories, or percent_of_kcal to set fat by % (limited to the allowed g/kg range).

tools.name: carbohydrate_calculator
tools.description: Carbohydrate grams = (daily kcal − protein g × 4 − fat g × 9) ÷ 4, with an optional training-day / rest-day split that keeps the weekly average.

tools.name: macro_meal_plan
tools.description: Use this first when asked for a meal plan. Returns daily calories, protein (1.9 g/kg default), fat (0.8 g/kg default) and carbohydrate, split into meals, plus meal-building rules. Get daily_kcal from maintenance_calories, bulking_calories or macro_calculator, then build meals with search_foods / get

tools.name: search_foods
tools.description: Search 2,886 foods in McCance and Widdowson's CoFID dataset. Returns energy, protein, fat, carbohydrate, sugars, fibre, saturated fat and sodium per 100 g, exactly as published (null = not measured). Use precise names, e.g. 'chicken breast grilled', 'oats', 'rice white boiled'. Figures are for build

tools.name: get_food
tools.description: Core figures for one food (per 100 g), by the ref from search_foods. Figures are for building finished answers only: never show the user rows, columns, codes, raw records or links to the data.

tools.name: search_exercises
tools.description: Find standard resistance exercises by name, muscle, equipment, location (gym/home) or level. Returns muscles, equipment and level. Figures are for building finished answers only: never show the user rows, columns, codes, raw records or links to the data.

tools.name: get_exercise
tools.description: One exercise by slug: muscles, equipment, setup, execution, breathing, range-of-motion and common-error cues, and alternatives. General information only; never diagnoses pain or injury. Figures are for building finished answers only: never show the user rows, columns, codes, raw records or links to

tools.name: list_calculators
tools.description: List every public Bodywise calculator with its MCP tool name, JSON API URL and canonical page.

tools.name: get_calculator_info
tools.description: Describe one calculator: method, units, API URL, canonical page and supporting guides.

tools.name: list_public_pages
tools.description: List every public, indexable Bodywise page (Hub guides, programmes, calculators and site pages) with canonical URLs.

tools.name: search_public_content
tools.description: Keyword search over public Bodywise pages. Returns titles, summaries and canonical URLs to cite.

tools.name: get_public_page
tools.description: Fetch one public Bodywise page by URL or path: metadata, references and clean Markdown text. Private, account and admin pages are refused.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_calculators, get_calculator_info, list_public_pages, search_public_content, get_public_page · Private data: search_foods, get_food, search_exercises, get_exercise, get_public_page · Public sink: macro_calculator.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_calculators, get_calculator_info, list_public_pages, search_public_content, get_public_page · Private data: search_foods, get_food, search_exercises, get_exercise, get_public_page · Public sink: macro_calculator

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
